info.title: Job Scheduler & Queue API
info.description:
Queue background jobs, follow their progress, and schedule them at runtime.

**Auth:** send `X-API-Key: <key>` on every request except `/health*` and `/metrics` (click *Authorize* above). Keys have scopes (`jobs:read`, `jobs:write`, `schedules:read`, `schedules:write`, `admin`) and may be limited to one tenant, some tasks, and a rate.

**Safe retries:** send an `Idempotency-Key` header on POST requests; repeating a request with the same key returns the original job or schedule instead of creating another.

**Errors:** every non-2xx response has the shape `{"error": {"status_code", "type", "message", "details"}}` — branch on `type`.

get.description: 200 whenever the API process is running. Checks no dependencies — use `/health/ready` for that.

200 only if the job database and the Redis broker both respond; otherwise
503 with each check's outcome in `error.details`. Point load-balancer
health checks here so traffic only reaches an API that can queue work.

post.summary: Queue one of every sample task
post.description:
Smoke test: queues every sample task, including one `flaky_task` that
always fails, so `GET /jobs?status=FAILURE` and `POST /jobs/{id}/retry`
have something to work on. That job reaches FAILURE only after its
automatic retries (up to about a minute with default settings).

post.description:
Queue `task_name(*args, **kwargs)`, with optional per-job settings:
`priority`, a delayed start (`delay_seconds` or `run_at`), `timeout_seconds`,
`max_retries`, and a `callback_url` webhook called when it finishes.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make retries safe.

**Errors:** `422` unknown task or arguments that don't fit it · `403` the
key may not run this task · `409` Idempotency-Key reused for a different request.

post.description:
Re-submit up to `limit` FAILURE jobs that haven't been re-submitted yet,
optionally only those of one `task_name` and/or with one exact `error`.
Each becomes a new job with `retry_of` pointing at the failed one.

Safe to repeat or to run twice at once: each failed job is re-submitted
at most once (an internal idempotency key per failed job).

get.description:
A [server-sent events](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Server-sent_events)
stream: one `status` event (the same JSON as `/status`) each time the
state or progress changes, then the stream closes after a final state
(SUCCESS, FAILURE, REVOKED). A `: keep-alive` comment is sent every 15 s.

Use it instead of polling, from a server (or a browser behind your own backend):

    curl -N -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" $API/v1/jobs/$ID/events

delete.summary: Cancel a queued, waiting or running job
delete.description:
Revoke the job. A queued (or delayed, or waiting workflow step) job will
never start, on any worker; a running one is terminated. In a workflow,
the steps that depend on it are skipped.

**Errors:** `404` unknown task_id · `409` the job has already finished
(SUCCESS, FAILURE or REVOKED).

post.description:
Create a schedule for any public task. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header
to make retries safe: a repeated request returns the original schedule
(200, `Idempotent-Replayed: true`) instead of creating a second one that
would fire the same job twice.

**Errors:** `422` if the task isn't public, the timing field doesn't match
`schedule_type`, `run_at` is in the past or has no timezone, the cron
expression is invalid, or `args`/`kwargs` don't fit the task's signature ·
`409` the Idempotency-Key was used for a different schedule, or the
tenant already has TENANT_MAX_ACTIVE_SCHEDULES enabled schedules ·
`403` the key may not run this task.

patch.summary: Pause, resume or retime a schedule
patch.description:
Change `enabled`, `interval_seconds` or `cron_expr`. A new timing takes
effect immediately: `next_run_at` is recalculated (last run + new
interval, or the next cron match from now). Resuming a schedule whose
`next_run_at` has passed fires it on the next poll.

A `once` schedule can't be retimed — delete it and create a new one.

**Errors:** `404` unknown id · `400` the field doesn't apply to this
schedule type · `409` resuming a `once` schedule that already fired, or
a system schedule · `422` invalid value.

Start the workflow and return it with every step's job (`task_id`).
Follow it with `GET /workflows/{id}`, or pass `callback_url` to be told
when it finishes. Steps may also have their own options (priority,
timeout, retries, callback).

unknown step ids, or a dependency cycle · `403` the key may not run a task ·
`409` Idempotency-Key reused for a different request.

ScheduleCreateRequest.title: ScheduleCreateRequest
ScheduleCreateRequest.description:
A dynamic schedule. Give exactly the timing field that matches `schedule_type`:

| schedule_type | required field     | behaviour                                      |
|---------------|--------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| `once`        | `run_at`           | fires once at that time, then disables itself  |
| `interval`    | `interval_seconds` | fires on the next poll, then every N seconds   |
| `cron`        | `cron_expr`        | 5-field cron, evaluated in **UTC**             |

One task may have any number of schedules.

WorkflowCreateRequest.title: WorkflowCreateRequest
WorkflowCreateRequest.description:
A set of steps that run in dependency order. Steps with no `depends_on`
start at once (fan-out); a step with several dependencies starts when all
of them succeed (fan-in). If a step fails or is cancelled, everything
downstream of it is skipped (REVOKED).
